name: Jake's Resume (LaTeX)
license: MIT (LICENSE, Copyright (c) 2020 Jake Gutierrez)
education_layout: 2x2 tabular: line 1 = bold Institution (left) | Location (right); line 2 = italic small Degree, Minor (left) | italic small date range (right)
experience_layout: 2x2 tabular: line 1 = bold Job Title (left) | date range (right); line 2 = italic small Company (left) | italic small Location (right); bullets below. Optional sub-heading for additional roles at same company: italic title | italic dates
skills_style: 'Label: items' categories, bold label then colon and comma list, one category per line (Languages, Frameworks, Developer Tools, Libraries)
contact_style: centered single line under name, items separated by ' | ' (phone | email | linkedin | github), links underlined
visual: full-width horizontal rule under each heading
project heading: bold project name | italic tech stack (left), date range (right)
date_format: Mon. YYYY -- Mon. YYYY (abbrev. with period e.g. 'Aug. 2018 -- May 2021', 'June 2020 -- Present')
notes: Very common ATS-friendly SWE format derived from sb2nov's resume. Experience swaps the line-2 order relative to education (title/date on line 1).

name: Awesome-CV (resume variant)
license: LPPL 1.3c (LICENCE file)
education_layout: cventry 2x2 table: line 1 = bold Institution (left) | italic colored Location (right); line 2 = small-caps gray Degree (left) | small slanted gray date range (right); bullet items below
experience_layout: cventry 2x2 table: line 1 = bold Organization (left) | italic accent-colored Location (right); line 2 = small-caps gray Job Title (left) | slanted gray date range (right); bullets below
skills_style: cvskills table: bold Category (left column) + comma list (right column), one row per category (Skills section is in the CV example, not the resume example)
contact_style: centered header; first name light + last name bold; position line in small caps accent color (items joined with ' · '); italic address line; social line with FontAwesome icons separated by ' | ' (mobile, email, homepage, github, linkedin); optional italic quote below
visual: very large name (32pt), first name light gray, last name bold
section headings 16pt bold with first 3 letters in accent color (awesome-red default)
section heading followed by a horizontal rule filling the rest of the line
subsections in small caps (e.g. Honors split into 'International Awards', 'Domestic Awards', 'Community')
footer with name, title, page number in small caps
date_format: Mon. YYYY - Mon. YYYY (e.g. 'Mar. 2010 - Aug. 2017')
notes: Honors section uses cvhonors rows: Award | Event | Location | Year. Accent color configurable (awesome-red, emerald, skyblue, etc.).

name: Deedy-Resume (OpenFonts)
license: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE)
education_layout: left sidebar: bold uppercase Institution line; small-caps Degree line; gray line 'Mon YYYY | City, ST' (date first, then location, pipe separated); optional extra lines (honors, GPA)
experience_layout: main column: bold UPPERCASE Company run-in with small-caps '| Job Title' on same line; next line gray 'Mon YYYY - Mon YYYY | City, ST' (left aligned, no right alignment); tight bullets below
skills_style: sidebar sub-groups: gray proficiency label (e.g. 'Over 5000 lines:', 'Familiar:') followed by items separated by bullet characters ' • '
contact_style: centered under name, one line separated by '|' (website | email | phone); separate sidebar 'Links' section with 'Github:// handle' style multi-line entries
visual: very large thin name (Lato Hairline/Light, 40pt), first name lighter than last
section headings uppercase, light weight, gray, 16pt, no rule
left sidebar ~1/3 width (Education, Links, Coursework, Skills), main column ~2/3 (Experience, Research, Awards, Publications)
awards as a 3-column table: year | rank | award
date_format: Mon YYYY - Mon YYYY or 'Mon YYYY - Present'
notes: Sidebar also has a 'Coursework' section (Graduate/Undergraduate subsections) not in the key list. Two-column layout is a classic ATS reading-order trap.

name: moderncv (template.tex; styles casual/classic/banking/oldstyle/fancy/contemporary)
license: LPPL-1.3c (README)
education_layout: cventry: date range in a narrow left column (right-aligned within it); main column one line: bold Degree, italic Institution, City, italic Grade (comma separated), description below
experience_layout: cventry: date range in left column; main column: bold Job Title, italic Employer, City on one line; description lines/bullets below. Subsections ('Vocational', 'Miscellaneous') allowed
skills_style: cvdoubleitem: two label/value pairs per row ('category: XXX, YYY, ZZZ'); languages via cvitemwithcomment 'Language  Skill level  Comment'; optional skill matrix with rating marks
contact_style: classic/casual: large name with title, contact items (address, phone, email, homepage, social) with icons, multi-line, aligned right in header (classic) or in footer (casual); banking: centered single line with separators
visual: colored section headings with a colored bar in the left column
color themes: blue (default), black, burgundy, green, grey, orange, purple, red, cerulean
date_format: year--year (template placeholder), free text
notes: Template also has 'Master thesis', 'Extra 1/2', 'References' sections. Style-specific header details (classic vs banking) are from general familiarity with the package; headings/macros verified from template.tex.

name: RenderCV 'classic' theme
license: MIT (rendercv/rendercv LICENSE)
education_layout: 3 columns: bold Degree in narrow left column; main = '**INSTITUTION**, AREA' then summary/highlights; right column = Location over Date
experience_layout: main = '**COMPANY**, POSITION' then summary and bullet highlights; right column = Location (line 1) over Date (line 2); time span shown in experience
skills_style: 'Label: items' categories, one per line, label bold (one_line_entry)
contact_style: centered single line with icons, no separator characters, items spaced 0.5cm
visual: large bold name 30pt in blue rgb(0,79,144)
section titles bold blue with partial line (rule after text)
footer 'NAME -- PAGE/TOTAL', top note 'Last updated in ...'
date_format: Mon YYYY – Mon YYYY (abbrev. months, en dash, 'present')
notes: RenderCV section titles are arbitrary YAML keys (snake_case keys are title-cased, e.g. selected_honors -> 'Selected Honors'); headings/order here are from the shipped John_Doe example YAML, which also has 'Patents' and 'Invited Talks' sections. Skills use one_line_entry template '**LABEL:** DETAILS'. Default single_date 'MONTH_ABBREVIATION YEAR', date_range 'START_DATE – END_DATE' (en dash), month abbreviations Jan..May, June, July, Aug, Sept...; 'present' for ongoing.

name: JSON Resume theme 'even'
license: MIT (LICENSE)
education_layout: h4 Institution; meta line 'StudyType in **Area**'; next meta line date range with duration; optional 'Courses' sub-heading + list
experience_layout: h4 Position (title first); meta lines: '**Company** · description', then date range + duration, then location (stacked, not right-aligned); consecutive roles at same company grouped under company name

contact_style: masthead: name h1, label/tagline h2, summary paragraph, then icon list (map-pin location, mail, phone, link, social profiles) stacked vertically on wide/print
visual: section headings in a narrow left gutter column, right-aligned, colored (secondary color); content in right column

notes: Section keys follow JSON Resume schema (basics, work, volunteer, education, projects, awards, certificates, publications, skills, languages, interests, references); heading 'References' also exists. Not a sidebar layout: headings sit in the left grid column level with their content, so plain-text extraction usually stays in order. Summary is unheaded (inside masthead).

license: University career guide; structure only, no content copied
education_layout: items: Institution, Location, Graduation Date, Degree(s), Major(s), Minor(s)/Concentration(s), GPA; optional Awards/Scholarships, Course Highlights (layout not specified)
experience_layout: not specified; result-focused bullets, reverse chronological

notes: Rule: Heading, Objective (if included) and Education come first in that order. Advises against templates.
